items.readme:
# chat-demo

English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

A static chat demo powered by the DeepSeek API. No application backend is required: the browser connects directly to the configured API service.

You can [try the app online](https://deepseek-ai.github.io/chat-demo/) or download the archive from [Releases](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-chat-demo/releases), extract it, and double-click `index.html` to use it locally without installation or a build. Enter your API key in Settings before your first chat.

## Getting started

Install Node.js 22.12+ and pnpm, then run:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/chat-demo.git
cd chat-demo
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

Open http://localhost:8090.

To build the static site:

```sh
pnpm build
```

The output is written to `dist/`. Deploy it to a static web server or open `dist/index.html` directly. Opening the file directly requires browser support for storage on `file://` pages and an API service that permits their cross-origin requests.

## Features

- Multiple conversations with automatic titles, renaming, and deletion; edit prompts, regenerate replies, and switch between message branches.
- Streaming replies, deep thinking, smart search, link reading, and source citations; stop generation or continue eligible replies.
- Upload, paste, or drag and drop attachments; use voice input and read replies aloud. A live audio spectrum appears in the first row of the input area while recording on mobile.
- Markdown, syntax highlighting, KaTeX math, and Mermaid diagrams.
- Simplified Chinese and English, light and dark themes, mobile layouts, location settings, and chat history import and export.

## Data and storage

Your API key and settings are stored in the browser's localStorage. Conversations and original attachments are stored in IndexedDB. Local data is isolated by browser profile and site origin. Sending messages, uploading attachments, and using speech features sends the relevant content to the configured API service.

History import and export in Settings use ZIP archives. After confirmation and successful validation, importing replaces all local conversations and attachments. Exports include conversations and locally available original images, but exclude API keys, settings, and original non-image attachments. See the [history import/export documentation (Chinese)](src/services/chat/history/README.md) for the archive format and preservation details.

Settings → Data → Delete all chats clears all local conversations, original attachments, and unsent drafts after confirmation. It stops ongoing replies and returns to a new chat. Your API key and settings are preserved; files already uploaded to the API service are not deleted.

## Development

| Command       | Description                  |
| ------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `pnpm dev`    | Start the development server |
| `pnpm build`  | Build into `dist/`           |
| `pnpm type`   | Run TypeScript type checks   |
| `pnpm lint`   | Lint with oxlint             |
| `pnpm format` | Format with oxfmt            |

[rspack.config.ts](rspack.config.ts) uses `https://api.deepseek.com` by default. Use `createConfig({ apiOrigin, devServer })` to customize the API origin and development server proxy.

Chat uses `deepseek-flash` by default through Anthropic-compatible Messages / Files APIs. Speech features use ASR / TTS endpoints. Requests include extensions for search, link reading, titles, and `latest_reminder`, so the configured service must support the corresponding capabilities. Supported attachment formats are determined by server-side validation.

```text
src/
  app/                 Application layout, themes, and global styles
  components/          Chat, settings, Markdown, and other UI components
  i18n/                English and Chinese translations
  services/
    api/               API requests, SSE, and protocol types
    chat/              Conversations, message branches, storage, and history import/export
    markdown/          Markdown parsing, syntax highlighting, and diagrams
    speech/            Audio recording and read-aloud playback
  utils/               Shared utilities
```

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). The build copies the license to `dist/LICENSE`; include it when distributing the app. Third-party dependencies are subject to their own licenses.

items.readme: # Apex Neural Rendering (ANR) [Apex Neural Rendering](https://apexcompute.com/neural-rendering) by [Apex Compute](https://apexcompute.com). - **ANR FG**: frame generation. In beta. - **ANR SR**: super resolution (upscaling). Beta soon. - **ANR RR**: ray reconstruction (denoising for ray tracing). Beta soon. - **Source code**: coming soon. - **nr-record**: records a game's frame generation or upscaler inputs to compare ANR FG, NVIDIA DLSS-G, DLSS, FSR, XeSS and others ([below](#record-and-compare-frame-generation)). Source in this repository. ## ANR FG Beta 1. Download a package from [Releases](../../releases): - `anr-fg-full`: for games without OptiScaler. - `anr-fg-addon`: for games that already use [OptiScaler](https://github.com/optiscaler/OptiScaler). 2. Close the game, extract the package and run the installer with the folder of the game's `.exe`: - Windows: `install.cmd` - Linux and Steam Deck (Proton): `sh install.sh ""`, then set the game's launch options to the line it prints: `WINEDLLOVERRIDES="dxgi=n,b" %command%`, or `winmm=n,b` in Vulkan games 3. In the game, turn on frame generation (the NVIDIA option where the game offers several). To uninstall, run `uninstall.cmd` or `sh uninstall.sh` with the same folder. ## Supported GPUs - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 20, 30, 40 and 50 series, and GTX 16 series - AMD Radeon RX 5000, 6000, 7000 and 9000 series, and Steam Deck - Intel Arc A and B series On Windows 10 and 11, and on Linux and SteamOS with Proton. ## Results and problems Please post them as [issues](../../issues/new/choose): - **Performance results**: run the test kit from the release and attach its result file. - **Problems**: the game, GPU and driver, operating system, settings and what you saw, with the newest `nr_fg-*.log` from under the game's `OptiScaler/custom/Apex Neural Rendering FG` folder. OptiScaler is GPL-3.0; its source for each release is attached to the release. ## Record and compare frame generation nr-record records the inputs a game gives its frame generation, losslessly. You can then replay a recording through any frame generation DLL you have (ANR FG, a game's DLSS-G `nvngx_dlssg.dll`) and compare the results as videos or images. nr-record includes no frame generation. Requirements: - a D3D12 or Vulkan game with DLSS frame generation, with the `anr-fg-full` package installed (it includes OptiScaler); - Windows 10 or 11, or Linux with Proton; - [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html) and ffprobe on the `PATH`; - for DLSS-G replays, an NVIDIA RTX 40 or 50 series GPU. 1. **Install.** Download `nr-record-1.2-windows.zip` or `nr-record-1.2-linux.tar.gz` from the [FG-V.B18 release](../../releases/tag/FG-V.B18) and extract it. Close the game and run the installer with the folder of the game's `.exe`: - Windows: `install.cmd ""`. No launch option is needed. - Linux and Steam Deck (Proton): `sh install.sh ""`. Set the game's Steam launch options to `WINEDLLOVERRIDES="dxgi=n,b" %command%` (the ANR FG installer prints the same line). Do not set this on Windows: the game may not start. The installer copies `nr-record` into `OptiScaler/custom/` and sets `FGNvngxReplacement=nr-record` in `OptiScaler.ini` (it keeps the original). When you are not recording, ANR FG generates the frames, or DLSS-G if ANR FG is not installed (`forward` in `nr-record/dlssg/nr_record.ini`). `uninstall.cmd` or `sh uninstall.sh` with the same folder removes nr-record and restores `OptiScaler.ini`. To install by hand: copy `capture/OptiScaler/custom/nr-record` into `OptiScaler/custom/`, set `FGNvngxReplacement=nr-record`, and set `forward` to `..\..\Apex Neural Rendering FG\dlssg\nvngx_dlssg.dll` or `nvidia`. 2. **Record.** Turn on DLSS frame generation in the game. **F6** starts and stops a recording; **F9** records the next 8 frames. Each start and stop beeps. While recording, the game shows only real frames. Recordings go to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\nr-record\` (Windows) or `~/.local/share/nr-record/` (Proton). A frame takes about 26 MB at 3840x2160 and 6 MB at 1806x972. `nr-record/dlssg/nr_record--.log` lists what was recorded. To record the upscaler's inputs instead (super resolution, D3D12 games): open OptiScaler's menu (**Insert**), pick `nr-record` in the upscaler list, and press **F6** to start and stop. It upscales with the upscaler `OptiScaler.ini` names (DLSS on NVIDIA, else FSR, or XeSS) and records that output too. Pick your upscaler again afterwards. Replay these recordings with `--generator dlss`, `fsr` or `xess` ([replay](record/replay/README.md#sr-and-rr)). 3. **Replay.** On Windows, in the package folder (`REC` is a recording's folder): ```bat tools\nr-record.exe info REC tools\nr-replay.exe --record REC --out out\anr --generator provider --dll "\nvngx_dlssg.dll" --label "ANR FG" --stream - | tools\nr-video.exe video - --out out\anr.mp4 tools\nr-replay.exe --record REC --out out\dlssg --generator nvidia --dll "\nvngx_dlssg.dll" --label DLSS-G --stream - | tools\nr-video.exe video - --out out\dlssg.mp4 tools\nr-video.exe project out\anr.mp4 out\dlssg.mp4 --out out\cmp.compare.json --labels "ANR FG" DLSS-G ``` On Linux, one command runs both replays under Proton's Wine and writes both videos, a side-by-side video and the compare project: ```bash python3 tools/nr_replay_wine.py --record REC --out cmp --video \ --generator provider --dll "/nvngx_dlssg.dll" --label "ANR FG" \ --b-generator nvidia --b-dll "/nvngx_dlssg.dll" --b-label DLSS-G ``` For images, replay with `--raw` instead of `--stream` and run `nr-video png`. 4. **Compare.** `viewer/renderer --compare --project cmp/compare.json` (Windows: `viewer\renderer.exe --compare --project out\cmp.compare.json`) plays both videos in sync, with a divider, side by side view, pixel zoom and marks, and exports videos and images. From the command line: `--compare-export PROJECT --out FILE --very-high`. `viewer/renderer --captures` lists your recordings and regenerates their frames with each generator. Docs: [recording](record/README.md), [format](record/FORMAT.md), [replay and videos](record/replay/README.md), [viewer](renderer/README.md). Build: `bazel build //record:nr-record //record/replay:nr-video //renderer`; Windows parts: `bazel build --config=windows_cross //record/capture:package //record/replay:nr-replay`. ## Citation ```bibtex @software{apex_neural_rendering, author = {{Apex Compute}}, title = {Apex Neural Rendering (ANR)}, year = {2026}, url = {https://github.com/apex-compute/ANR}, note = {https://apexcompute.com/neural-rendering} } ```

Erosion-CN

基于 worse_query 的 iOS / iPadOS 系统配置与 MobileGestalt 研究工具箱（中英双语 · 防白苹果安全加固版）

支持 iOS / iPadOS 27.0 – 27.2 / 27.3 beta 1（完整支持）以及 iOS / iPadOS 26.x（部分支持）。

简体中文 · English Documentation · AppleFlow 配套分流与排雷台

  

--- ## 项目简介 **Erosion-CN** 衍生自上游 **[jailbreakdotparty/Erosion](https://github.com/jailbreakdotparty/Erosion)**，提供中英双语界面，修复了原版多项真机 Bug，并做了防白苹果安全加固： - **修改重启不反弹**：原位覆盖写入（`pwrite` + `F_FULLFSYNC`），保留系统文件 Inode 与属主，不注入 iOS 27 非缓存键。 - **防相机黑屏**：Plist 编辑器精确保留布尔值与浮点类型，未修改项原样直通。 - **写入安全**：应用前逐项预览变更，写后全量读回校验，不一致自动回滚。 - **零硬编码偏移**：运行时解析本机 `libMobileGestalt.dylib`，动态计算 `CacheData` 槽位（`green-tea`、`wapi` 等），校验不通过即锁定写入。 - **原厂双备份 + 一键恢复**：沙盒与系统金库双重 `SHA-256` 备份，卸载重装不丢，可一键还原原机出厂参数。 - **国行 Apple 智能解锁**：完整美版 `LL + LL/A` / 仅改 `LL` 双模式，四要素体检与一键配齐修复，真机生效核验探针，`SiriHub`、`Audio Intelligence` 等坑位自动防呆。 - **国行底层限制解除**：FaceTime 音频、境外 eSIM、「无线局域网」显示为「Wi-Fi」。 - **实用工具**：应用存档备份、缓存清理、跨容器文件浏览、语音备忘录无损导出、电池与崩溃诊断，以及 Surge / Stash 分流规则一键导出。 > 📜 完整的技术改进说明与版本历史见 [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md)，各版本发布说明见 [Releases](https://github.com/Kianuni/Erosion-CN/releases)。 > 📖 外部独立底层架构解析：[《从 worse_query 逃逸到 MobileGestalt 运行时重构：深入 Erosion-CN 的防白苹果原位写入、双重金库与国行底层解锁架构》](https://lijianfei.com/post/erosion-cn-ios-system-configuration-mobilegestalt-architecture/) --- ## 系统兼容性 > [!IMPORTANT] > 操作前请务必通过电脑完整备份设备重要数据！修改系统底层配置存在潜在风险，仅供安全研究与学习交流，请仅在本人持有的设备上使用并自行承担风险。 - **iOS / iPadOS 27.0 – 27.2.1**、**27.3 beta 1**（完整支持所有功能，包括 `MobileGestalt` 读取与安全写入） - ⚠️ **`27.3 beta 1` 国行生成式功能限制**：写入与绝大多数功能正常，但国行（`CH/A`）硬件上**照片「高质量消除 / 扩图 / 重构」、相机 `SIRI` 等生成式云端功能会被系统本地拦截**（日志：`Eligibility returned no CN region policy on a CH region code device`），改 `MobileGestalt` 无法绕过，详见 FAQ Q6「情况 C」。需要这些功能请留在 / 降回 `27.2.x`。 - **iOS / iPadOS 26.0 – 26.7.2**（部分支持：可使用锁屏壁纸、拨号键盘美化、锁屏底部签名文字与部分容器浏览；受底层沙盒限制，iOS 26 不支持写入系统 `MobileGestalt`） --- ## 安装与签名要求 > [!WARNING] > 本项目底层依赖至少一个有效的 `App Group` 容器权限。请使用支持保留或注入 App Group 的个人 Apple ID 自签工具（如 **SideStore / AltStore / Feather / Sideloadly / Impactor / iLoader**）或带 App Group 权限的开发者证书签名安装。 ### 方式一：订阅官方自动更新源（推荐 · 支持一键升级） 在 iPhone / iPad 浏览器中点击下方按钮即可一键添加官方软件源（每次新 Release 发布自动同步，内含 `App Group` 权限声明与 `SHA-256` 校验）：

手动添加官方源地址（兼容 SideStore / AltStore / Feather / LiveContainer / ESign）： ```text https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kianuni/Erosion-CN/main/apps.json ``` ### 方式二：手动下载 IPA 签名安装 1. 前往 [Releases 页面](https://github.com/Kianuni/Erosion-CN/releases/latest) 下载最新的 `Erosion_v0.9.1_Bilingual.ipa`。 2. 使用上述签名工具安装至设备；首次运行可在「主页」日志确认已成功识别 `App Group`。 3. 详细使用说明与原厂状态恢复教程请查阅： - 📘 [USAGE_GUIDE.md（安装与使用指南）](./USAGE_GUIDE.md) - 🔄 [RESTORE_CHA.md（无损恢复出厂状态指南）](./RESTORE_CHA.md) --- ## 常见问题与排障指南 (FAQ / Q&A) ### Q1：为什么打开了开关，eSIM 还是没生效？或者国行 18 Pro / 18 Pro Max 改完后「添加 eSIM」反而消失了？ 请按以下 6 种情况逐一排查： 1. **国行 iPhone 18 Pro / 18 Pro Max（`A3715` / `A3718`）插着双实体卡（或背面副卡）触发基带卡槽冲突（18 系列最常见！）** 国行 18 Pro / Pro Max 为特殊的**「正反双实体 SIM 卡槽 + 内置 eSIM」三通道复用硬件**，而美版 `LL/A`（`A3472` / `A3473`）为无卡槽纯 eSIM 机型（国际版也仅正面单卡槽）。若卡托内插着两张实体卡（或插在卡托背面副卡槽）重启，基带检测到卡槽占用冲突会临时隐藏「添加 eSIM」与 `EID`（或导致背面副卡不工作）。 ✅ **真机实测 100% 解决与双实体卡共存步骤（「空卡写卡法」）**： - ① **先拔出 SIM 卡托（不插任何实体卡，保持空卡状态）**，在 Erosion-CN 开启「解除地区限制」+「解除国行底层限制」点击应用后 **空卡关机冷重启**（注：若在 `27.3 beta 1` 空卡下仍隐藏入口，可先关闭上方地区限制、**仅单开「解除国行底层限制」空卡重启**，「添加 eSIM」必出）； - ② 空卡开机连 Wi-Fi（挂外区节点 + 开启飞行模式），扫码把需要的海外 eSIM 全部添加完毕； - ③ **插回实体卡策略**：若平时只需 **1 张实体卡 + 多张海外/国内 eSIM**，将实体卡装在卡托**正面（主卡槽）**即可直接共存；若平时还需使用**卡托背面第 2 张实体卡**，写完海外 eSIM 后进 Erosion-CN **单独关闭「解除国行底层限制」（保留上方「解除地区限制」开启，且自 `v0.8.1` 起还可在下方修改模式切换为「仅改区域代码 LL（保留 CH/A 后缀与双卡兼容）」以保留原厂 `CH/A` 与监管型号）**，应用重启后再插回正反双实体卡——背面实体卡即可恢复工作，且已写入芯片的海外 eSIM 依然完整保留、可随时在设置中切换启用！ 2. **只点了「注销 (Respring)」，没有「手动关机重启」** 「解除国行底层限制」修改的是二进制 `CacheData`（`green-tea` 槽位）。负责蜂窝基带与 eUICC 芯片的守护进程（`CommCenter`、`ctkd`）在注销桌面时**不会重载缓存**，甚至会因新旧区域参数半同步导致「添加 eSIM」入口临时隐藏。**写入后必须手动滑动关机、等待黑屏后再按电源键开机（冷重启）** 才会生效。 3. **只改了 `LL/A`，漏开了「解除国行底层限制 (eSIM / FaceTime 音频)」** 常规解锁必须将 **「解除地区限制（国行 AI / 美版 LL/A）」** 与下方的 **「解除国行底层限制 (eSIM / FaceTime 音频)」** **两个开关同时打开**并冷重启；若只改了上方的 `LL/A` 而未解开下方的 `green-tea` 硬件锁，系统校验区域冲突同样会屏蔽 eSIM 菜单。 4. **误开了「机型伪装 (`ProductType`)」或曾用其他改机工具盲改过缓存** 原生 AI 机型**严禁修改机型标识符**（如把国行主板 `iPhone19,7` 强改成美版 `iPhone19,3`），否则基带校验失配会导致整个 eSIM 菜单消失。若之前被其他工具改坏，请点击 `MobileGestalt` 右上角 **`⋯` →「清除并重建缓存」** 并重启恢复纯净原厂基线，再重新按需开启开关。 5. **在中国大陆境内扫码添加海外 eSIM 时提示“不支持 / 无法激活”** 若「添加 eSIM」按钮已出现，但扫码瞬间被拦截，是系统激活时通过境内基站/定位触发了位置校验。扫码写卡时请开启 **飞行模式 + 连接 Wi-Fi（挂全局海外代理）**（必要时临时关闭 `设置 → 隐私与安全性 → 定位服务 → 系统服务` 中的「蜂窝网络搜索 / 无线局域网与蓝牙」），写卡成功后再恢复正常即可长期双待使用。 6. **老款纯双实体卡槽国行机型的物理硬件限制** 仅自带物理 `eUICC` 安全芯片的国行机型（如 **国行 iPhone Air、内置物理 eSIM 的 iPhone 18 系列** 等）支持解锁海外 eSIM 自由扫码；早期**纯双实体 nano-SIM 卡槽且主板物理空焊 `eUICC` 芯片**的常规国行机型属于硬件缺失，开启该开关仅用于解锁 **FaceTime 音频（语音通话）** 与 AI 区域准入，无法凭空生成物理 eSIM 芯片。 ### Q2：需要开启「监管模式 (Supervision)」吗？以前别的工具留下的伪监管怎么清理？ * **完全不需要，且严禁在个人零售设备上开启伪监管！** Erosion-CN 的所有解锁均直接安全作用于 `MobileGestalt` 缓存，零监管依赖。 * 许多早期改机工具注入的伪造 `CloudConfigurationDetails.plist` 缺失合法的 MDM 证书链，一旦后续 OTA # mcp-for-blender-pro

### Your Blender scene. Your AI models. One creative workspace.


**An AI assistant for Blender that can inspect your scene, build objects, edit materials, find assets and carry out multi-step workflows—with a visual chat workspace and a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.**


![Blender 4.2+](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blender-4.2%2B-E87D0D?logo=blender&logoColor=white)
![Release 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-1.0.0-98D85B)
![Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/download-Windows_x64-357EC7)
![MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)


[Download](https://github.com/hitkeeen/blender-ai-mcp-addon/releases/latest) · [Getting started](docs/QUICKSTART.md) · [Connections and agents](docs/CONNECTIONS.md)


![AI chat workspace with a live Blender scene preview](docs/images/studio.png)


## Turn a creative brief into scene operations


Start with an idea. Ask the assistant to inspect your scene, create a product-display layout, arrange objects, assign materials or prepare an export. Follow its actions in the conversation and inspect the result in the viewport preview. Keep working in Blender throughout the process.


**mcp-for-blender-pro brings conversation, scene tools, model choice and agent workflows together.** It is designed for artists who want faster iteration, technical artists who automate repetitive work, and developers connecting AI tools to Blender.


## Why choose mcp-for-blender-pro?


| Capability | What it gives you |
|---|---|
| **Blender-aware assistance** | Scene and object inspection gives the assistant context before it acts. |
| **A visual Studio workspace** | Chat, scene objects, viewport snapshots, approvals and a task board in a companion window. |
| **Your choice of AI** | Connect supported cloud providers, local Ollama models or compatible custom endpoints. |
| **Saved connections** | Keep work and personal connections separate, including multiple keys for the same provider. |
| **One assistant or a team** | Use a single model for quick changes, or managers, workers and reviewers for structured tasks. |
| **Built-in MCP server** | Connect OpenCode and other clients supporting authenticated Streamable HTTP MCP. |
| **21 scene tools** | Create, inspect, edit, capture, search assets, consult Blender APIs and export scenes. |
| **Multilingual menus** | Choose English, German, French, Spanish or Chinese for the main interface. |


## From a quick edit to an agent team


Use **Single assistant** for direct, conversational work. For larger tasks, configure a **Team chain** with individual responsibilities, instructions and models.


- **Manager:** breaks the request into assignments and acceptance criteria.
- **Workers:** perform the assigned scene operations.
- **Reviewers:** inspect results and approve work or return specific findings.


Tasks run sequentially so scene edits stay ordered. A blocked task gets one correction attempt; a second failed review stops the workflow. The task board exposes assignments, attempts and review findings as work progresses.


![Agent roles and model configuration](docs/images/studio-team.png)


## Connect the models that fit your work


Supported connections include **OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, OpenCode Zen, Ollama and custom APIs**. Load the available model catalog and select a model directly in Blender or Studio.


Custom endpoints support OpenAI Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages and Ollama protocols. Choose models with tool-calling support; image-capable models can also interpret viewport screenshots. OpenCode-only free models are available through the OpenCode client.


![Provider, saved connection and model selection](docs/images/studio-settings.png)


## Install and create


1. Download **`mcp-for-blender-pro.zip`** from [Releases](../../releases/latest).
2. In Blender, open **Edit → Preferences → Get Extensions → menu → Install from Disk**.
3. Select the ZIP, enable **mcp-for-blender-pro**, then open **3D Viewport → N → MCP Pro**.
4. Choose a provider, add your connection details and select a model.
5. Send a message in Blender or click **Open Studio Window**.


The release bundle targets **Windows x64 with Blender 4.2 or later**. Keep Blender open while using Studio or an external client.


### Try these prompts


> Inspect this scene and explain its object structure before making any changes.


> Create a simple product-display scene with a pedestal, a camera and three lights. Give the pedestal a matte blue material.


> Duplicate the selected object into a neatly spaced row of five and show the viewport.


> Find an appropriate Poly Haven asset for this scene and ask before importing it.


## Blender automation through MCP


Launch **OpenCode Portable** from the sidebar to work through OpenCode with the Blender connection configured for you. OpenCode manages its own provider sign-in and model selection. Other compatible MCP clients can connect to the authenticated local endpoint described in the [connection guide](docs/CONNECTIONS.md).


| Tool group | Included tools |
|---|---|
| Scene inspection | `get_scene_info`, `list_objects`, `get_object_info` |
| Object creation | `add_cube`, `add_sphere`, `add_cylinder`, `add_plane`, `add_light`, `add_camera` |
| Editing | `move_object`, `duplicate_object`, `delete_object`, `parent_objects`, `set_material` |
| Visual feedback and scripting | `viewport_screenshot`, `execute_code` |
| Blender API and export | `bpy_api_lookup`, `describe_node_type`, `export_scene` |
| Asset workflows | `search_assets`, `import_asset` |


Asset integrations include **Poly Haven, Sketchfab and Poly Pizza**. Configure service keys where required and follow the licenses of the assets you use.


## Stay in control of your scene


Built-in chat supports operation approvals, cancellation after the current step and named undo steps for mutations. Python tool validation helps catch disallowed operations; it is not a security sandbox. External MCP clients manage their own approval policies.


Connection credentials are stored in your user settings. Chat history lasts for the current session. Studio runs locally and authenticates requests to Blender.


## Keywords

Private AI meeting notes. A free, open-source alternative to Granola.

Download for Mac · Windows · Linux

Yogurt records your calls without adding a bot to the meeting.

macOS 14.4+ (Apple Silicon) · Windows 10 2004+ (x64) · Ubuntu 22.04+ or similar (x64 AppImage) · 8 GB memory

yogurt.so · Help · Build and run locally · MIT license

Made by Frigade.

## What it does - **Live transcripts.** Yogurt records calls and turns speech into text as you talk. - **Meeting summaries.** Yogurt writes up the conversation and any notes you add. - **Private by default.** Your audio, transcripts and AI processing stay on your computer. - **Free and open source.** You can use Yogurt without an account. - **Who said what.** Yogurt names speakers from Zoom, Teams and Meet on Mac only. - **Languages.** Multi-language mode transcribes 99 languages. - **Recording reminders.** Yogurt offers to record when a supported call starts. - **Answers with sources.** Yogurt answers questions across meetings and links to the source. - **Folders and search.** You can find meetings by folder, title, notes or transcript. - **Copy and export.** You can copy notes or transcripts, or save both as Markdown. - **Local MCP server.** Your chosen assistant app can read your notes when you allow access. - **Automatic stop.** Yogurt stops recording when the call ends. ## Watch the demo https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da16b894-beb1-491a-89e1-fd10666dc9b8 ## How it works 1. **Record.** Start recording your microphone and call audio; you can add your own notes. 2. **Transcribe.** Yogurt uses whisper.cpp and, on supported Macs, Apple SpeechAnalyzer. 3. **Summarize and ask.** A local open-weight model runs through llama.cpp. Meeting data stays local; Yogurt goes online for model downloads and update checks.
Where your meetings, recordings, settings and models are stored - Mac uses `~/Library/Application Support/Yogurt`. - Windows uses `%APPDATA%\Yogurt`. - Linux uses `~/.config/Yogurt`, or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/Yogurt` if set.
## FAQ
What kind of computer do I need?
> A Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14.4 or newer, a 64-bit PC with Windows 10 (version 2004) or newer, or a 64-bit Linux computer with Ubuntu 22.04 or newer. Each needs at least 8 GB of memory. If your computer is too slow, Yogurt tells you during setup. Calendar and speaker names from calls are Mac only for now.
Windows says “Windows protected your PC.” What do I do?
> Click More info, then Run anyway. Windows shows this for new apps that aren’t signed with a Microsoft certificate yet. Yogurt is open source, so anyone can check what it does.
Does Yogurt join my meetings?
> No. Yogurt records your microphone and the sound playing on your computer. No bot joins the call, so let the other people on the call know you’re recording.
Are recordings saved?
> Yes. Your recordings, transcripts, and notes are saved locally on your computer.
Is Yogurt free?
> Yes. Yogurt is free and open source under the MIT license. No account is needed.
Does Yogurt work offline?
> Yes. After a one-time download of the AI models, transcription and summaries run locally on your computer.
How much does setup download?
> It depends on your computer. Yogurt downloads a smaller notes model first, about 5 GB, then the best one your computer can run well, which can be 14 GB or more. Recording works once setup finishes, and notes and questions work offline once the notes model is in.
How do I connect my assistant app?
> In **Settings → AI apps**, turn on access, copy the helper command, and add it as a local MCP server in your assistant app. Access is off by default. The app can read your meetings, notes and transcripts, but cannot change them. It may send what it reads to its own online model. Turn access off in Yogurt to stop further reads.
Can other apps read my notes through MCP?
> Access is off until you enable it in **Settings → AI apps**. Apps get read-only access to meetings, notes and transcripts. Mac and Linux use a socket in your profile folder with `0600` permissions, so only your user account can open it. Windows uses a named pipe with a new random name each launch, stored only in your profile folder. There is no per-app token, so any app running under your account can read while access is on. Settings shows connected apps by their self-reported names.
Which AI models does Yogurt use?
> Transcription uses Whisper through whisper.cpp, with large-v3-turbo or a smaller model depending on your computer. On supported Macs, Apple SpeechAnalyzer supplies live words while Whisper produces the saved transcript. Summaries and answers use a local open-weight model from the Gemma 4, gpt-oss or Qwen3 families, chosen for your hardware and run through llama.cpp. The app uses Electron and needs no account.
Which languages does Yogurt support?
> Pick **Multi-language** in **Settings → Language → Spoken language** to transcribe 99 languages. You can also switch from the **English** menu in a note’s footer before or during recording. English only is the default. Summaries follow the meeting’s main language; answers follow your question’s language. Settings also offers 32 app languages.
Which call apps does Yogurt work with?
> You can record calls in any app because Yogurt captures your microphone and system audio. Call detection covers Zoom, Teams and Meet. On Mac, Yogurt can also read their speaker names with Accessibility permission, when the call app shows who is speaking.
How does Yogurt know a call has started?
> It checks which apps are using your microphone. For browser calls, it also checks the tab title or a nearby calendar event with a call link. This triggers an offer to record; recording starts only when you choose to.
How do I connect my calendar?
> On Mac, allow Calendar access in Settings. Yogurt reads the calendars already on your computer and lets you choose which ones to show. You do not sign into a calendar account in Yogurt.

# SuperMimic

[Project page](https://supermimic.github.io) | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28480)

SuperMimic trains a humanoid whole-body motion tracker with one differentiable world model, built on [mjlab](https://github.com/mujocolab/mjlab).

## Setup

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

Clone both repos as siblings:

```bash
mkdir supermimic_ws && cd supermimic_ws
git clone git@github.com:HybridRobotics/supermimic.git
git clone git@github.com:HybridRobotics/mjlab_research.git
cd supermimic
```

## Usage

Available task IDs:

- `SuperMimic-GenCoord-G1` — generalized coordinates representation
- `SuperMimic-MaxCoord-G1` — maximal coordinates representation

Train a world model and policy:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<GPU_ID> uv run src/supermimic/scripts/train.py \
  <TASK_ID> --runner.run_name <description>
```

Play back a trained model:

```bash
uv run src/supermimic/scripts/play.py \
  <TASK_ID> --wandb-path <RUN_PATH>
```

## Acknowledgements

SuperMimic contains code inspired by these projects:

- [ControlVAE](https://github.com/heyuanYao-pku/Control-VAE) (BSD-3-Clause)
- [robotic_world_model](https://github.com/leggedrobotics/robotic_world_model) (Apache-2.0)
- [DreamerV3](https://github.com/danijar/dreamerv3) (MIT)

## License

items.readme:
# Abyssal Garden

**A dreamy underwater world you can swim through, right in your browser.**

Towering kelp forests, sunbeams pouring through a rippling surface, a sunken ship, manta rays gliding overhead.
And all of it is made by code: no images, no 3D models, no sound files. The whole world fits in **one 96 KB HTML file**.

![Kelp forest with a stone whale tail and a manta ray](.github/screenshots/whale-fluke.jpg)

## Try it

1. Download [`index.html`](index.html).
2. Open it in **Chrome** or **Edge** on a desktop computer.
3. Wait a few seconds while the world is built, then press **Dive in** and start swimming.

Nothing to install, and it works offline. It needs a browser with **WebGPU**. If you see *"This scene needs WebGPU"*, update your browser or switch to Chrome / Edge.

## What's down there

- **Kelp forests** that sway in the current and sparkle with tiny gold and green specks
- **Light rays** streaming down from a wavy surface, with shimmering caustics on the sea floor
- **A sunken wooden ship**, a **giant stone whale tail**, rock arches, canyons and floating boulders
- **Manta rays**, schools of fish, rising bubbles and drifting particles
- **A purple grotto** with glowing magenta ground cover, coral and barrel sponges
- **A soundscape** made up as you listen: a deep rumble, distant whale calls, soft chimes and bubbles

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Shipwreck](.github/screenshots/shipwreck.jpg) | ![Looking up through the kelp](.github/screenshots/kelp-forest.jpg) |
| ![Barrel sponges](.github/screenshots/sponge-garden.jpg) | ![Light rays over the kelp basin](.github/screenshots/light-rays.jpg) |

![The purple grotto](.github/screenshots/purple-grotto.jpg)

## Controls

| | Keyboard & mouse |
|---|---|
| Look around | Move the mouse |
| Swim | `W` `A` `S` `D` |
| Up / down | `E` / `Q` |
| Swim faster | Hold `Shift` |
| Jump to a viewpoint | `1` to `6` (the spots in the screenshots) |
| Menu | `Esc` releases the mouse and opens the menu with the list of controls; **Resume** takes you back |
| Sound on / off | `M` (sound starts when you dive in) |
| Performance stats | `H` |
| Detail level | **Low**, **Medium** or **High** in the menu (reloads the page) |

The seabed, cliffs and arches are solid: you glide along the rock instead of swimming into it, and you still fit through every tunnel and arch. Kelp, plants, corals, sponges, loose rocks, the floating boulders, the ship and the whale tail you can swim through.

**On a touchscreen:** hold one finger down to swim forward and slide it to steer. Put a second finger down to go faster. The `≡` button in the corner opens the menu. Phones always show the scene in landscape and start on Low or Medium detail. (Touch support is experimental.)

## Detail levels

The **Low**, **Medium** and **High** buttons in the menu pick the detail level; the current one is lit. Each level is the same world, built with less in it:

| Level | What it is | Picked on a first visit for |
|---|---|---|
| **High** | The full scene | Computers |
| **Medium** | Half of the leaves, sparkles and pebbles; small rocks, sponges and corals cast no shadows | Phones with 8 GB of memory |
| **Low** | A quarter of the leaves, no anti-aliasing, coarser rocks and corals, simpler lighting, 480p to start with | Other phones, and computers with 4 GB of memory or less |

If loading crashes the tab, or the graphics driver gives up, the page starts again one level lower. Your browser remembers the level, and the resolution and draw distance the scene settled on, for the next visit.

## How it works

- The seabed is sculpted on your graphics card every time the page opens, then decorated with about two million kelp leaves and plants, tens of thousands of rocks, and thousands of sponges, corals and fish.
- Everything is drawn with **WebGPU** directly. No game engine or 3D library is used.
- The ship, whale tail, mantas, fish and corals are built from simple mathematical shapes.
- The sound is synthesized live with the Web Audio API.
- It's built to run smoothly: about 180 fps at 2560×1440 on an RTX 5070 Ti. On slower hardware it aims for 60 fps by lowering first the resolution and then how far away plants and rocks are drawn, in small steps. The scene is already running, blurred, behind the start menu, so most of that tuning is done before you dive in. A low-end phone (Samsung Galaxy A16) reaches about 20 fps at 670×372 on Low.

## Make it your own

The readable source code is in the [`source`](source) folder. To change something and rebuild `index.html` you need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 18 or newer:

```bash
cd source
npm install
npm run build
```

This writes a new `index.html` next to this README. `npm run build:readable` writes an unminified version instead, which is easier to debug in the browser's developer tools.

`npm run build:dev` writes a separate `dev.html` with two extra tools that are not part of `index.html`: `F` flies the camera along a one-minute path through the whole world, and `B` runs that flight as a benchmark and reports frame and GPU times.

| File | What's inside |
|---|---|
| [`source/src/world.js`](source/src/world.js) | The world layout: rock walls, arches, tunnels, kelp forests, sponge gardens, fish schools, mantas, the ship and the whale tail. **A good place to start.** |
| [`source/src/shaders.js`](source/src/shaders.js) | The look: water and fog colors, lighting, kelp, rocks, the water surface and light rays (WGSL shader code) |
| [`source/src/main.js`](source/src/main.js) | The renderer, the camera, the controls, the six viewpoints and the camera path the world is laid out around |
| [`source/src/audio.js`](source/src/audio.js) | The soundscape |
| [`source/src/quality.js`](source/src/quality.js) | The detail levels: which one a device starts on, and what is remembered between visits |

items.readme:
# muse.ai 注册 / 邀请码兑换 协议分析

补充一下，记得用JP 节点， JP 不需要绑卡，直接过

纯 HTTP 实现 muse.ai 的注册与邀请码兑换流程，不依赖浏览器。本文记录的是通过抓包逐字段比对得出的协议细节。

## 快速开始

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp config.example.json config.json   # 填入邮箱与可选代理
python example_register.py
```

## 目录结构

```
musepy/
  client.py    注册 + 兑换的完整协议客户端
  runner.py    多账号批量调度（sticky 代理 / 预算 / 停止语义）
  otp.py       验证码轮询（幂等：只取 send 之后的最新码）
  falco.py     行为埋点上报（可选）
  caa.py       注册漏斗事件上报（可选）
example_register.py        单账号端到端示例
example_batch.py           多账号批量示例
config.example.json        配置模板
test_onboarding_smoke.py   离线冒烟（披露解析纯函数）
test_runner_smoke.py       离线冒烟（批量调度，mock 网络）
```

## 协议流程

```
GET  /                                   拿初始 cookie
POST /api/auth/native/restart            → 201 {csrf_token}
POST /api/auth/native/send-otp           → 201
POST /api/auth/native/confirm-otp        → 200 {registration_state:"completion_required",
                                               tos:{content_version}}（动态 TOS 版本）
POST /api/auth/native/register-completion→ 200 {auth_meta_session:{frl_access_token, frl_account_id}}
POST auth.meta.com/hatch/session/bootstrap/ → 302…→ muse.ai 200 HTML（会话引导，必须）
     └ 从 muse.ai 文档解析动态披露 disclosure_text/disclosure_version 与状态门
       （resolvedDestination/isGeoGated/waitlist → 地区受限）
POST /api/hatch/accept-tos               → 200（单次调用；正文用服务端动态披露，非硬编码）
GET  /api/hatch/invite                   → 200 表示账号有效
POST /api/hatch/vm/wake                  → 200（必须，否则兑换误报 invalid；
                                             wake_trigger=mount + open_id + away_ms=0）
POST /api/hatch/stateful-sharing         → 200
POST /api/hatch/invite-code/redeem       → 200 {redemptionStatus:"redeemed"}
POST /api/hatch/invite                   → 200 {code}（取回自己的码，不等于页面刮开 reveal）
```

## 几个容易踩的坑

### 1. `confirm-otp` 必须带 `supports_muse_link_transparency: true`

```json
{"otp_code":"123456","remember_device":true,"supports_muse_link_transparency":true}
```

### 2. `register-completion` 的姓名字段语义

```json
{
  "date_of_birth": "1993-11-14",
  "first_name": "三郎",     // 名（given name）
  "last_name": "近藤",      // 姓（family name）
  "tos_content_version": "ntm_create_account:default_v1_meta_account_v3+docs_v2",
  "remember_device": true
}
```

`first_name` 是名、`last_name` 是姓，与直觉相反。生日早于约 18 年前会返回 403——同一会话同一份姓名，只把生日从 2013 改成 1993 就能从 403 变 200。

### 3. `restart` 的 body 不是空对象

```json
{"resume": false}
```

### 4. `accept-tos` 是会话激活开关，且必须先引导会话

注册完成后**必须先走 `POST auth.meta.com/hatch/session/bootstrap/`**（form 表单只带
`frl_access_token`，手动跟随 302/301/303 跳转落到 muse.ai 200 文档），否则后续
hatch 接口一律 403。引导落地的 muse.ai 文档里带有 Next Flight 序列化的动态披露
（`disclosureText` / `disclosureVersion`，当前实测版本为 `HATCH_ROW_v0`），`accept-tos`
的正文必须用服务端返回的这份动态文案（**不是**硬编码常量），`Referer` 用披露页
URL；单次调用即可，不重试，403 时把响应体前 200 字符带出来便于诊断。

引导后若服务端判定 `resolvedDestination == "waitlist"` 或 `isGeoGated == true`，
属于**地区受限**：注册已完成、账号保留，但未证明已加入名单。

### 5. `vm/wake` 缺失会让兑换误报

不调 `vm/wake` 直接兑换，即使是有效码也会返回：

```json
{"success":false,"reason":"invalid","detail":"この招待コードは存在しません"}
```

需要先从已登录页面提取 `vmId`：

```python
re.search(r'vmId[\\"]*:[\\"]*([0-9a-fA-F-]{36})', html)
```

`wake` 的 body 实测为：`wake_trigger: "mount"`（首连）、`open_id`（新 uuid）、
`away_ms: 0`，而不是早期的 `resume`。

### 6. 兑换失败原因的含义

| reason | 含义 |
|---|---|
| `redeemed` | 成功 |
| `already_redeemed` | 本账号已经兑换过一个码 |
| `used_up` | 该码达到 30 次使用上限 |
| `invalid` | 码不存在，或没调 `vm/wake` |

## Cookie

注册成功后 `hatch_sess` 由 `register-completion` 的响应头下发（约 886 字符），这是后续所有 hatch 接口的凭证。`hatch_vml` 在注册阶段一直是被清空状态（`Max-Age=0`），不属于必需项。

## 多账号批量（musepy/runner.py）

```bash
python example_batch.py [count]
```

`config.json` 里的批量字段：

| 字段 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `otp_file` | 邮箱清单，每行 `email----otp源URL`（otp 源返回 `[{"otp","time"},...]` JSON） |
| `proxy_file` | sticky 代理池，每行 `host:port:user:pass`（或 `host:port`） |
| `codes_file` | 可选，待兑换邀请码池，每行一个 |
| `output_dir` / `tried_file` | 每账号结果 JSON 目录 / 已尝试邮箱清单 |
| `workers` / `max_per_ip` | worker 数（默认 5）/ 每条代理的验证成功上限（默认 6） |
| `resolve_ip` | 是否通过 ipify 解析出口 IP（默认 true） |
| `send_caa` | 批量模式下是否上报注册漏斗埋点 |

调度语义（与本地实现一致，不承诺任何绕过行为）：

- **worker 独占 sticky 代理**：一条代理行同一时刻只归一个 worker（claim/release），
  不抢他人的行；代理池耗尽才共享并打日志。
- **max_per_ip 按验证成功数计**：达到上限释放当前行并换另一行，原行本轮避开。
- **pre-send 传输失败重试**：`bootstrap`/`restart` 等**未发出 OTP 前**的网络失败，
  释放当前代理并**同邮箱换代理重试，上限 3 次**，不消耗新邮箱；仍失败标记 tried。
- **业务拒绝 / pending / 已发 OTP 后的失败：整批停止**——不换行、不重试、不补号。
- **region_waitlist**：账号已注册但地区受限——记录 `registered_waitlist`、账号保留，
  整批停止。
- **预算 = 领取的不同邮箱数**：失败不补号；结束打印 batch_summary JSON
  （queued/started/remaining/ok/pending/server_rejected/transport_error/failed/
  ip_switches/stopped/stop_reason）。

每账号结果写入 `output_dir/<email>.json`，字段：`email/status/stage/registered/
own_code/own_code_status/reveal_status/is_revealed/ip/last_error`。
`frl_access_token` 与 `hatch_sess` 仅在内存中使用，**不落盘**。

OTP 轮询幂等：每次 `send_otp` 前记录开始时间，`musepy/otp.py` 只取该时间之后的
最新 6 位验证码（45 秒超时、0.6 秒间隔、单请求 15 秒超时）。

## 埋点说明

站点前端会上报两类遥测：

- **falco**（`POST /api/falco`）—— 性能指标与业务交互事件，`machineId` 固定为 `not_set`
- **caa-events**（`POST /api/auth/caa-events`）—— 注册漏斗，通过 `navigator.sendBeacon` 逐步骤上报，同一 `waterfall_id` 贯穿全程

两者都不参与注册判定，缺省不影响流程能跑通。`musepy/falco.py` 与 `musepy/caa.py` 保留了完整实现，可通过配置关闭。

## 使用声明

本项目仅供个人、非商业的学习与研究使用，不采用 MIT 等开源许可证。不得用于商业用途或再分发。实际使用时请遵守目标站点的服务条款与当地法律法规。

items.readme:
# 遥测清理 · TelemetryCleaner > 运营商为终端入网、自注册、网络运维和故障排查，确有在相应场景收集必要数据的实际需求！本项目仅供学习，用于了解 Android 系统包管理机制。 TelemetryCleaner 可以检测国行 Android 固件预置的运营商组件，查看各空间的安装状态和权限，并管理卸载与恢复。下载： [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Eynnzerr/TelemetryCleaner/releases/latest)

您可通过不限于以下方式参与贡献，欢迎 PR： 1. 提供清单未覆盖的厂商+运营商+包名线索，在 README.md 中补充即可； 2. 提供针对某模块的实测与分析报告，不限制是否为 AI 生成，但需保证真实性。放于 docs 目录中即可； 3. ~协助实现未支持的免 Root 卸载功能（如**现版本不支持部分 vivo 系的电信/移动组件卸载**）~； 4. 对软件功能的反馈或改进。 ## 背景介绍 部分国产厂商在国行固件中预置了 `SystemHelper`、`RegService` 等运营商终端管理组件。这些组件在后台静默定时采集数据，用户无感；没有桌面入口，同时无法以常规手段禁用权限和卸载。 WiSec 2023 的流量测量还在部分国行样机上观察到运营商组件上报数据，其中小米及 ColorOS 样本的中国移动组件上报了已安装软件列表。 [WiSec 2023 实测论文](https://www.scss.tcd.ie/Doug.Leith/pubs/wisecfp034-liu.pdf#page=7) 在作者本人的 OPPO 真机上观测到 SystemHelper 有读取定位、设备和 SIM 标识、已安装应用以及按应用统计网络流量，随后向某云端上传的行为，分析详见 [SystemHelper 代码与权限分析 by AI](docs/reports/oppo-telemetry-components.md)。 ## 本项目原理 Android 10 及以上设备可安装本项目，依赖 Shizuku。先按 [Shizuku 启动指南](https://shizuku.rikka.app/guide/setup/)通过 ADB 或无线调试启动 Shizuku，再回到 App 授权并选择需要检查的空间。Android 11 及以上可用无线调试启动。检测完成后，可打开组件详情查看权限，或勾选组件批量操作。 ADB 启动的 Shizuku 以 shell 身份代理 Binder 调用。App 直接请求系统包管理服务，避开部分 ROM 对 `pm` 命令行入口的拦截。系统包管理服务仍会执行本机的权限和包状态校验。 [Binder 调用实现](app/src/main/java/com/eynnzerr/telemetrycleaner/data/PackageBinder.kt) 少数 ROM 会在命令层直接拒绝卸载系统应用，例如返回 `Failure [only root can delete system app for a particular user]`。收到这类系统错误后，App 会以 shell 身份通过 `app_process` 调用隐藏的 `IPackageManager.deletePackageAsUser` 再试一次；重新读取包状态确认失败后，结果页仍显示原始系统错误，不会用兜底流程的错误信息覆盖它。 [app_process 兜底实现](app/src/main/java/com/eynnzerr/telemetrycleaner/data/PackageFallback.kt) 卸载按选定空间执行，会清除该空间中的组件数据。恢复使用系统保留的 APK。自动清理默认关闭，开启后按配置的周期检查所选空间，只处理自动清理名单内的组件。 **已知限制：vivo OriginOS 的 PMS 底层中，电信/移动组件 com.vivo.devicereg 被列入了 vivo 系统保护名单，暂无法在非 Root 情况下完成卸载。其他厂商经实测反馈均支持。** ## 内置组件清单 表中的「未验证」指尚无本人在相应厂商设备上的卸载验证。 | 厂商 | 运营商 | 包名 | 卸载验证 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 跨厂商 | 联通 | `com.mobiletools.systemhelper` | 已实测 | | OPPO / 一加 / realme | 电信 | `com.oppo.ctautoregist` | 已实测 | | OPPO / 一加 / realme | 移动 | `com.coloros.regservice` | 已实测 | | 小米 / Redmi / POCO | 电信 | `com.xiaomi.registration` | 已实测 | | 小米 / Redmi / POCO | 移动 | `com.miui.dmregservice` | 已实测 | | vivo | 移动 / 电信 | `com.vivo.devicereg` | 暂不支持 | | 华为及旧荣耀 | 电信（数据） | `com.huawei.android.UEInfoCheck` | 已实测 | | 华为及旧荣耀 | 电信（短信） | `com.huawei.android.AutoRegSms` | 已实测 | | 华为 | 移动 | `com.huawei.regservice` | 已实测 | | 荣耀 | 电信（数据） | `com.hihonor.android.UEInfoCheck` | 已实测 | | 荣耀 | 电信（短信） | `com.hihonor.android.AutoRegSms` | 已实测 | | 荣耀 | 移动 | `com.hihonor.regservice` | 已实测 | | 魅族 / Flyme | 移动 | `com.meizu.regservice` | 已实测 | | 初代红魔 | 电信 | `cn.nubia.register` | 未验证 | 本人只验证了 SystemHelper 和 OPPO 组件的卸载，小米、华为由网友验证实测。其他厂商因缺少设备暂未验证，如决定卸载，请自行承担风险。 欢迎在 [Issues](https://github.com/Eynnzerr/TelemetryCleaner/issues) 反馈某厂商某模块卸载后使用正常，也欢迎补充组件。附上机型、系统版本、包名和实际结果，便于复核。 ## WIP - [ ] 努比亚、国行三星、魅族运营商遥测组件包名收集 - [ ] 扩充更多组件检测（包括厂商自己的敏感数据收集组件）作为可选项 - [x] 部分 vivo 系不支持卸载 SystemHelper 外的组件。暂提供冻结策略作为兜底

items.readme:
资源雷达 · Resource Radar

全网福利、黑五好价、拼车交易、开源项目与新闻资讯的多兴趣自托管聚合雷达站

五大内容形态分流 · 21 类分频道目录 · 统一屏蔽词省额度 · AI 语义定级 · 多路由精准推送

简体中文 · English

--- **资源雷达（Resource Radar / repo: `freebie-radar`）** 是一款轻量、开箱即用的多兴趣社区信息聚合与精准推送工作台。它从各大开发者社区、游戏平台、软件限免站、GitHub、Reddit、Bluesky、Telegram 频道及自定义 RSS 采集信息，并通过 **「规则初筛与统一屏蔽 → AI 语义定级与分流 → 分频道目录呈现 → 多路由精准推送」** 把每条内容送到它该去的位置： - 只想纯粹蹲羊毛？首页默认 **「真福利精选」** 严格锁定 AI 验真的 `freebie`（直接白嫖 + 实操可领的有条件福利），绝不被付费好价、拼车、二手或新闻污染。 - 想看 **黑五 VPS 好价 / 合规拼车 / 开源项目 / 重大新闻与科技资讯**？一键切换顶部兴趣频道即可浏览各自专属的下级分类、真实有效计数与图文卡片，并可分别配置互不干扰的 Telegram 专题推送路由。 --- > 在线演示： --- ## 界面预览 | 工作台列表视图（多兴趣频道栏 + 跨源折叠 + 兑换码一键复制） | 三列图文卡片视图（零额外请求封面图提取 + 响应式 2列/3列网格） | | :---: | :---: | | ![工作台列表视图](docs/ui-public.png) | ![三列图文卡片视图](docs/ui-grid.png) | | 多路由精准推送（分形态/分类/获取方式/关键词定制即时或攒批路由） | AI 语义引擎（21 类分流、自适应学习与零 Token 存量重整分类） | | :---: | :---: | | ![多路由精准推送](docs/ui-push-panel.png) | ![AI 语义引擎](docs/ui-ai-panel.png) | --- ## 核心特性 ### 1. 多兴趣频道与「形态 × 领域 × 获取方式」正交分类 - **5 大内容形态（`kind`）**：`freebie`（白嫖福利）、`deal`（特价好价·含黑五 VPS/拼车/二手出鸡）、`opensource`（开源项目）、`info`（新闻资讯·指南）、`noise`（纯求助/灌水噪音）。 - **21 个垂直领域（`category`）**：覆盖 `ai`（AI 额度）、`vps`（VPS/主机）、`cloud`（云服务）、`domain`（域名/建站）、`opensource`（开源软件）、`software`（软件授权）、`dev`（开发/工程）、`design`（设计/素材）、`security`（安全/网络）、`hardware`（硬件/数码）、`media`（影音会员）、`game`（游戏）、`carpool`（拼车/合租）、`trade`（二手/交易）、`headline`（时政/要闻）、`finance`（财经/商业）、`news`（综合快讯）、`goods`（实物/优惠/话费券）、`invite`（邀请码）、`edu`（教育/电子书）、`other`（其它）。 - **分频道自适应下级分类**： - 「真福利精选 / 完全白嫖」只展现福利类目（隐藏拼车/交易/新闻要闻），统计数字实时排除 `noise` 假数； - 「新闻资讯」自动切换为资讯栏目视角（时政/要闻、财经/商业、AI 前沿、开发工程、开源生态、安全/漏洞、硬件数码、综合快讯）； - 切换频道自动重置不兼容的形态、获取方式与价格上限，避免空屏串态。 - **6 级获取方式（`obtain`）**：严格区分 `free`（直接白嫖）、`conditional`（有条件）、`lottery`（抽奖）、`trial`（试用/Demo）、`promo`（推广/引流）、`paid`（需付费）。 ### 2. 三层高信噪比治理（统一屏蔽 · AI 定级 · 零 Token 重整） - **统一屏蔽词防火墙（省额度 + 隐网页 + items.description: A Claude skill and TypeScript library for animated line-art SVG components: ink figures that walk and react, scenes with a day/night cycle.
items.readme:
# line-art-animation

A Claude skill and a small TypeScript library for animated line-art components:
ink-on-paper figures that walk, ride and react, in scenes that run from day to night.
Everything is drawn live in SVG, so it stays sharp at any size and responds to the
pointer.

![A Japanese street drawn in line art, going from late afternoon to night](media/village.gif)

| Day | Night |
|---|---|
| ![The village at midday](media/day.png) | ![The village at night with lit windows](media/night.png) |

## What's in the repo

| | |
|---|---|
| `SKILL.md`, `references/` | The skill: workflow, the rules that make the style work, and guides for style, motion, scenes, verification, matching a reference clip and rendering video. |
| `lib/` | Four dependency-free TypeScript modules: drawing primitives (`ink.ts`), a walk/run solver (`gait.ts`), springs, pendulums and wind (`motion.ts`), and a time-of-day palette (`daynight.ts`). |
| `examples/walker/` | One figure in about 150 lines: a man with a briefcase walks across the card; click him and he tips his hat. |
| `examples/village/` | A full scene: a street of machiya, a tea house and a bath house by a canal, villagers on schedules, a cat, birds, a boatman, lit windows and reflections, about a dozen interactions. |
| `scripts/` | Deterministic frame capture for video, and tools for measuring a reference clip. |

## Install the skill

For Claude Code, clone it into your skills folder:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/JDhruv14/line-art-animation ~/.claude/skills/line-art-animation
```

or into `.claude/skills/` inside a single project. Then ask for what you want, for example:

- "Make a line art animation of a bakery at dawn: a baker carrying trays, steam from the oven, a cat in the window."
- "Turn this clip into a looping line-art component, matching its walk exactly." (attach or link the clip)
- "Add a day-night cycle to the scene and render a 30-second 1080p video."

Claude reads `SKILL.md`, copies `lib/` into your project, shows one figure for approval
before building the rest, and checks motion frame by frame before handing it over.

## Run the examples

Requires Node 22.18 or newer.

```sh
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173
```

In the village, drag the sun or moon across the sky to change the time, move the pointer
to make wind, and click people, windows, lanterns, the wind chime, the cat, the birds or
the water. URL flags: `?start=0.9` sets the starting time (0 is midnight, 0.5 noon),
`?tau=0.5` pins it, `?day=30` makes a full day last 30 seconds, `?debug` steps time by hand.

```sh
npm run typecheck  # strict for lib/ and the walker
npm run build
```

## The library in brief

![The walker example: a man with a briefcase and a red scarf walking past a lamp post](media/walker.gif)

Figures are drawn in their own space, about 95 units tall with feet on y = 120, and placed
into a scene with a transform. Limbs are two open pen strokes around a curve through the
joints, which is most of what makes the drawing read as hand-inked.

A complete program that draws a pair of legs walking across the page (the walker
example adds the body, arms, clothes and the click reaction):

```ts
import { el, limb, shoe, place, inkDefs, run } from './lib/ink.ts';
import { gait } from './lib/gait.ts';

const svg = el('svg', { viewBox: '0 0 480 240' });
document.body.append(svg);
const fig = el('g', { filter: inkDefs(svg).filter }, svg);
const legs = [limb(fig, 4.2), limb(fig, 4.2)];
const shoes = [el('path', {}, fig), el('path', {}, fig)];

const walk = gait({ kind: 'walk' });
let phase = 0, x = 60;
run((t, dt) => {
  phase += dt / walk.period;
  x += walk.speed * 1.25 * dt;           // move at the gait's speed and the feet stay planted
  place(fig, x % 520 - 20, 196, 1, 1.25);
  const p = walk.pose(phase);
  p.feet.forEach((foot, i) => {
    legs[i].draw([p.hip, foot.knee, foot.ankle]);
    shoe(shoes[i], foot.ankle, foot.pitch);
  });
});
```

`gait()` solves the legs rather than animating them: the planted foot slides back at
exactly the travel speed, the swing follows a minimum-jerk path, the heel peels off the
toe before each step, and hip height comes from what the planted legs can reach, so the
body rises over each step and dips when both feet are down. Clothes are then drawn
around the knees and ankles, so a coat or kimono opens and closes with the stride.

`palette(τ)` gives sky, paper and ink colours for any time of day. Ink is `currentColor`
and paper fills carry a `pp` class, so `applyPalette()` can turn the whole drawing into
pale ink on indigo at night while windows and lanterns glow.

## Render a video

```sh
npm run dev
node scripts/capture.ts "http://localhost:5173/examples/village/?debug&capture&day=30&start=0.3" \
  captures/village 900 30 1920 1080
ffmpeg -framerate 30 -i captures/village/f%04d.png -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 15 \
  -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart -tune animation village.mp4
```

The capture script drives headless Chrome over the DevTools protocol, with no npm
dependencies, and advances the scene by exactly one frame between screenshots, so the
result doesn't depend on machine speed. It finds a local Chrome or Chromium, or uses
`$CHROME`. Needs ffmpeg.

## Match a reference clip

```sh
node scripts/clip.ts period clip.mp4 X Y W H          # loop length of a region
node scripts/clip.ts blobs clip.mp4 X Y W H Y0 Y1     # dark blobs per frame, e.g. feet
scripts/frames.sh clip.mp4 X Y W H out/               # frames with a measuring grid
```

`references/matching.md` covers the rest: why to resample by time (most social clips
are variable-frame-rate), reading poses off the grid, and an overlay mode for checking
your drawing against the clip.

## License

MIT

items.readme: # islandcn A Dynamic Island-style component for any React app, installed with shadcn. Show an upload, a timer, a song, a ride on its way, an incoming call or a recording in one island at the top of your app, and shape each activity around your app's own actions. ```bash npx shadcn@latest add https://islandcn.dev/r/island-core.json ``` ```tsx "use client"; import { Island, IslandProvider, useIsland } from "@/lib/island"; // Mount once near the root. ; // Then, from any component inside it: const island = useIsland(); const upload = island.start({ id: "upload", label: "Uploading report.pdf", compact: { leading: , trailing: }, expanded: { center: report.pdf, bottom: }, }); upload.update({ compact: { trailing: } }); upload.end(); ``` ## What's here - **The engine** (`lib/island/`, registry item `island-core`): the activity stack, four presentations (idle, compact, the split, expanded), springs fitted to frame-by-frame recordings of the real island, long-press, alerts and reduced motion. React only. - **Presets** (`components/islandcn/`): upload, timer, now playing, incoming call, ride or delivery ETA, recording, nearby transfer, battery and the split, each one file on the engine, plus the content kit they share. - **The playground** (`/playground`): build an island for your app from a preset or a blank activity, fire every action, tune the motion and copy the install command and the code. - **The site and docs** (`app/`, `docs/content/`). Coding agents can use the optional `islandcn-skill` registry item as an install helper; see `/docs/agent-skill`. ## Develop ```bash pnpm install pnpm dev # http://localhost:3000 pnpm typecheck pnpm build # builds the registry into public/r, then the site ``` Read `AGENTS.md` before changing anything. The recordings the motion was fitted to are not in this repo. `/lab` still plays every transition from its built-in sequences in `pnpm dev`; `/compare`, which sets the web side against the recordings, has nothing to show, and the one test that reads them is skipped. ## License MIT, copyright (c) 2026 Leo. See `LICENSE`. islandcn copies the look and motion of Apple's island, but none of Apple's assets. It is not affiliated with Apple. Dynamic Island is a trademark of Apple Inc.

# FailSafe ARTEX

A source-built, locally bound distribution of [ARTEX](https://github.com/RuoJi6/ARTEX), an open-source multi-agent security testing harness. This repository exists because the prebuilt `tomicdd/artex` Docker image was found to contain an unauthenticated command-execution backdoor in November 2026. This build is compiled from the audited `v0.3.15` source tag and keeps upstream's full runtime capabilities, including Node 22, Playwright, Chromium, and nmap. The compose file binds the console to localhost and does not publish the recording proxy. > **Authorized testing only.** ARTEX runs an autonomous agent that can execute > shell commands and send network traffic. Use it only against systems you own > or have explicit written permission to test. ## Managed ARTEX runs FailSafe can host and run ARTEX safely for you using **GlassBreak**, our cyber-grade model. We handle the isolated runtime, scoping, evidence handling, and the operational controls that are easy to get wrong in a self-hosted deployment. If you want a managed run, contact us: - **Email:** [hello@getfailsafe.com](mailto:hello@getfailsafe.com) - **Contact form:** ## Quick start Requirements: Docker Engine with Compose v2, and about 5 GB of free disk (the browser stack and Chromium account for most of the image size). If your Docker installation only provides the standalone `docker-compose` command, substitute it for `docker compose` below; `make` detects either. ```bash cp .env.safe.example .env.safe chmod 600 .env.safe # edit .env.safe: set POSTGRES_PASSWORD and, optionally, an LLM key docker compose --env-file .env.safe -f docker-compose.safe.yml up -d --build ``` Open and complete the first-run setup. If you left the LLM key blank, configure a provider in the console before starting a scan. Check status and logs: ```bash docker compose --env-file .env.safe -f docker-compose.safe.yml ps docker compose --env-file .env.safe -f docker-compose.safe.yml logs -f artex ``` Stop without deleting data: ```bash docker compose --env-file .env.safe -f docker-compose.safe.yml down ``` Delete everything, including the database and ARTEX data: ```bash docker compose --env-file .env.safe -f docker-compose.safe.yml down -v ``` ## What is different from upstream | Area | Upstream default | This build | |---|---|---| | Image | prebuilt `tomicdd/artex` (backdoored) | compiled from this source tree | | Runtime user | root | root (upstream parity) | | Console binding | `0.0.0.0:8787` | `127.0.0.1:8787` | | Recording proxy | published on `8788` | not published | | Browser automation | Node 22 + Playwright + Chromium | same, pinned versions | | Browser MCP launcher | `npx @playwright/mcp` | pinned `playwright-mcp` | | Capabilities | default Docker set | default Docker set + `no-new-privileges` | | Self-update | points at upstream | points at this fork; one-click update disabled | | Base images | floating tags | pinned by digest | The API, UI, skills, browser MCP, and browser-driven recon are unchanged. Node, Playwright, the Playwright MCP/CLI, and Chromium are preinstalled; `nmap` raw scans and runtime `apt`/`npm -g` installs work because the container runs as root, as upstream does. The deployment hardening that remains is the loopback-only console, an unpublished proxy, `no-new-privileges`, a persisted JWT key, and digest-pinned base images. ## Build without Docker ```bash cd web npm ci --ignore-scripts npm run build:static cd .. rm -rf server/webui/dist mkdir -p server/webui/dist cp -R web/out/. server/webui/dist/ CGO_ENABLED=0 go build \ -trimpath -buildvcs=false -tags embedui \ -ldflags="-buildid= -X main.version=v0.3.15-failsafe.1" \ -o artex ./cmd/artex ``` Then run `./artex -addr 127.0.0.1:8787 -proxy 127.0.0.1:8788` with `ARTEX_PG_DSN` set to a PostgreSQL database you control. This bare-binary path does not install Node, Playwright, Chromium, or the recon CLI tools; use the Docker image for full upstream capability. ## Verify the build ```bash make verify ``` This checks the known implant indicators (`verifyCaptcha`, `tomicdd`, `congdonglinux`), prints the binary SHA-256, and lists the image ID. See [`audit/artex-v0.3.15-audit.md`](audit/artex-v0.3.15-audit.md) for the full audit of this tag. ## Data and secrets - `.env.safe` contains the database password and optional LLM keys. Keep it `0600` and out of version control. - The database lives in the `pgdata` volume; ARTEX data and evidence live in `artex_data`; the JWT signing key lives in `artex_key`. Back up all three. - ARTEX stores scan evidence, which may include credentials, tokens, and customer data. Treat `/app/data` and the database as sensitive. - For a backup, stop the stack and archive the volumes, or use `pg_dump` inside the `postgres` container. ## Updating Read [`UPSTREAM.md`](UPSTREAM.md) first. In short: review the upstream diff, rebuild, run `make verify`, update the audit report, and only then deploy. ## License and provenance ARTEX is AGPL-3.0. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE) and [`UPSTREAM.md`](UPSTREAM.md). This fork's modifications are released under the same license. The upstream README is preserved as [`README.upstream.md`](README.upstream.md).

# ai-texture-forge

**An AI-powered texture forge for Blender — turn text prompts into seamless PBR materials, concept art and scene-wide projections with local or cloud diffusion models, straight inside the 3D viewport on Windows.**

[download-url]: https://github.com/linknimiball1974/ai-texture-forge/releases

![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11-3776AB) ![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows-0078D6) ![Blender](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blender-4.2%2B-E87D0D) ![Stable Diffusion](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI-Stable%20Diffusion-8A2BE2) ![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-active-2EA44F)

[![Download](docs/download-button.svg)][download-url]

**The forge in one scene:** type `weathered copper, green patina, seamless` in the N-panel, pick a provider, and a tile-ready PBR set lands on the active object — color, roughness and normal maps wired in one click; one depth-aware projection later, the whole alley is skinned before the coffee cools.

## Why

Texturing from stock libraries is a grind: hours hunting for a texture that only sort of fits, seams stitched by hand in an image editor, round-trips through external AI tools that break your flow, and licenses that never quite cover the project. ai-texture-forge moves generation into the 3D viewport — you describe the surface, the forge renders it with a local GPU engine or a connected cloud provider, bakes seamless tiling, projects it across the scene by depth and wires the maps into Blender's shader nodes — so a project travels from blockout to fully textured render in one sitting without leaving Blender.

## Without / With

| Without | With |
|---|---|
| Hunting stock libraries for a texture that sort of fits | Type the surface you want and generate it on the spot |
| Seams stitched by hand in an image editor | The Seamless option bakes perfect tiling into every generation |
| Round-tripping through external AI tools and re-importing images | Generation runs inside the viewport and lands straight on the object |
| Skinning a whole scene object by object | One depth-aware projection textures the entire scene in a pass |
| Low-res outputs that fall apart in close-ups | AI upscaling lifts generations 4× with the detail intact |

## Quick Start

1. Download **`mcp-for-blender-pro.zip`** from [Releases](../../releases/latest).
2. In Blender, open **Edit → Preferences → Get Extensions → menu → Install from Disk**.
3. Select the ZIP, enable **mcp-for-blender-pro**, then open **3D Viewport → N → MCP Pro**.
4. Choose a provider, add your connection details and select a model.
5. Send a message in Blender or click **Open Studio Window**.

## Features

- **Generate from a text prompt** — textures, concept art and background assets from a plain description, with prompt presets that get the look right on the first try.
- **Bake seamless tiling** — the Seamless option produces textures that tile with no visible seam, ready for game and archviz surfaces.
- **Skin entire scenes by projection** — depth-to-image paints whole models and environments in a single pass.
- **Fix and extend with inpaint/outpaint** — repair blemishes and seams, or grow an image in any direction to widen a backdrop.
- **Upscale 4× with AI** — low-res generations come back crisp enough for close-ups.
- **Restyle renders** — the render pass and node system re-style stills and animations inside the compositor.
- **Choose your engine** — run diffusion locally on your GPU or connect a cloud provider, and keep every result in a history you can recall, export and import.

## How it works

ai-texture-forge runs as a single Blender add-on: the **N-panel** and **Studio Window** route your prompt to the **Provider Layer**, which drives a local **Diffusion Engine** on your GPU or a connected cloud API, while the **Texture Pipeline** handles seamless wrapping, depth projection, inpainting and 4× upscaling and the **Material Builder** wires the result into Blender's shader nodes as color, roughness and normal maps. The **History** store keeps every generation recallable, and the **external client** bridge keeps a remote session in sync while Blender stays open.

## Usage

- **Game-ready brick wall** — type "weathered red brick, mortar, seamless", enable Seamless and generate: the PBR set lands on the wall mesh with roughness and normal maps, tiling across the whole facade with no visible seam.
- **Concept art in the viewport** — block out a sci-fi alley, pick a concept preset and generate background assets straight into the camera view, iterating variants without leaving Blender.
- **Scene-wide projection** — select the environment, run a depth-aware projection with "abandoned factory, rust and dust" and the whole scene is skinned in one pass; inpaint the spots that need care, then upscale to final resolution.

## Configuration

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Provider | Local GPU | Diffusion backend: local engine or cloud API; endpoint URL and key live in the same panel |
| Model | — | Diffusion model used for generations |
| Resolution | 1024 | Base size of generated images |
| Steps | 30 | Diffusion steps per generation; more steps add detail and time |
| Seed | Random | Fix the seed to iterate on the same look |
| Seamless | Off | Bakes tiling into the result with no visible seam |
| Depth strength | 0.6 | How tightly the projection follows scene depth |
| Upscale | 4× | AI upscaling factor applied to final outputs |
| Render pass blend | 0.5 | Mix between the Cycles render and the restyled result |
| History | On | Recall, export and import past generations |

## Troubleshooting / FAQ

- **The ZIP will not install.** Windows marks downloaded files — run `powershell Unblock-File -Path "$HOME\Downloads\ai-texture-forge.zip"` and install again.
- **No ai-texture-forge panel in the sidebar.** Check `Edit → Preferences → Get Extensions`: the add-on must be enabled, and the bundle requires Blender 4.2 or later on Windows x64.
- **Generations fail or stall.** Verify the provider endpoint and key in the N-panel and confirm the model name; the local engine needs a supported GPU with enough VRAM, and a cloud provider can take over when it cannot.
- **Seams are still visible.** Enable Seamless before generating; inpaint can also repair the seams of an existing texture automatically.
- **Results look soft in close-ups.** Run the 4× AI upscale on the final generation — detail returns without a re-render.
- **The AI assistant does not respond.** Keep Blender open — Studio and external clients talk to a running Blender session.

## Contributing

Prompt presets, provider configs and workflow ideas are welcome — open an issue or a pull request. If ai-texture-forge saves you a stock-library hunt, tap the **★ Star** button: it helps other artists find the forge.

items.readme:
Run Cloudflare Workers anywhere: AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, or your own servers.

The same developer experience, without the runtime limits, for a fraction of the bill.

Docs · Deploy · Migrate · Bindings · Examples · Discord

## What is OpenOrange OpenOrange runs your existing Cloudflare Workers project on AWS, Google Cloud, Azure or your own servers, with no changes to your code. It's built with four goals: - **Zero refactoring, zero-downtime migration**: your Workers and Durable Objects run as they are, and your data moves off Cloudflare while your app keeps serving. - **The same developer experience**: `wrangler dev` becomes `orange dev`, and everything underneath is open source and self-hostable. - **Simpler bills**: you pay for the machines you run on, not Cloudflare's metering or an enterprise contract. Compute is 4.8× cheaper and storage 8.7× cheaper. - **Built for scale**: storage is backed by S3, so scaling out is a matter of adding machines. ## Quickstart You need a Worker project with a `wrangler.jsonc`, `wrangler.json`, or `wrangler.toml` (or use [`examples/hello-durable-object`](examples/hello-durable-object)), Node.js 22 or later, and pnpm. Deploying also needs Docker. ### Use a coding agent Paste this into your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …) from your Worker project: ```text First, add the Rivet MCP (https://mcp.rivet.dev/mcp) to this agent, and ask me to approve the Rivet sign-in. Then run this project's Cloudflare Worker on Rivet with OpenOrange: ask me where it should run (on my machine, on a Rivet cluster, or on my own Rivet Engine), read https://github.com/rivet-dev/open-orange/blob/main/README.md and follow its quickstart. Do not change my app code. ``` ### Step 1: Install Install the `orange` CLI globally, then run it in your Worker project. Your code and your Wrangler configuration do not change. ```sh pnpm add -g open-orange ``` ### Step 2: Run your Worker Your Worker answers on `http://localhost:8787`. Each Durable Object runs as a Rivet Actor with its own SQLite database, kept in `.open-orange/`. ```sh $ orange dev Binding Resource Runs on env.COUNTER Durable Object Rivet Actor · Counter ● Ready in 4.6s Local http://127.0.0.1:8787 ``` ### Step 3: Deploy `orange deploy` builds an image of your Worker and rolls it out to a Rivet cluster, then prints its public URL. ```sh $ orange login $ orange link --cluster $ orange deploy ✓ Deployed my-worker URL https://api.example.com ``` See the [deploy guide](https://openorange.dev/docs/deploy/), or [self-host it](#self-host). ## Migrate your data without downtime `orange migrate` moves your Durable Objects off Cloudflare with zero downtime.

See the [migration guide](https://openorange.dev/docs/migrate/) for every step, rollback, and what cannot move. ## Run it where you want Next to your database, in the cloud and region you choose. - **Rivet Cloud**, fully managed: a dedicated cluster on AWS or Google Cloud, in the region you choose. Operated by Rivet. - **BYOC**, your cloud and our ops: your AWS, Google Cloud or Azure account. Operated by Rivet over an outbound connection. - **Self-hosted**, open source under Apache 2.0: any cloud, Hetzner, on-prem or air-gapped. Operated by you. ### Self-host 1. **Build the Docker image.** `orange deploy --dry-run` writes the build and calls no API. Push the image to a registry your servers can pull from. ```sh orange deploy --dry-run --outdir out docker build --platform linux/amd64 -f out/Dockerfile -t my-worker out/context ``` 2. **Run the Rivet control plane.** Follow Rivet's guide for your platform: [Kubernetes](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/control-plane/kubernetes/), [AWS ECS](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/control-plane/aws-ecs/), [Docker Compose](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/control-plane/docker-compose/), [Hetzner](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/control-plane/hetzner/), [Railway](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/control-plane/railway/), [Render](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/control-plane/render/), [a VM](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/control-plane/vm/). 3. **Run your image as worker nodes.** Point each container at the control plane with `RIVET_ENDPOINT`, following Rivet's guide for your platform: [Kubernetes](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/nodes/kubernetes/), [AWS ECS](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/nodes/aws-ecs/), [Docker Compose](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/nodes/docker-compose/), [Hetzner](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/nodes/hetzner/), [Railway](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/nodes/railway/), [Render](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/nodes/render/), [a VM](https://rivet.dev/docs/deploy/self-host/nodes/vm/). See [self-hosting](https://openorange.dev/docs/deploy/#self-host) in the deploy guide. ## How pricing compares Cloudflare's meters, priced on raw AWS: Graviton EC2 in us-east-1 with 40% headroom, and S3 in your account. See [the cost model](https://openorange.dev/#cost). | | Cloudflare | OpenOrange | | |---|---|---|---| | Durable Object compute | $0.045 per GB-hour | $0.0094 per GB-hour | 4.8× cheaper | | Durable Object storage | $0.20 per GB-month | $0.023 per GB-month | 8.7× cheaper | | SQLite writes | $1.00 per million rows | about $0.18 per million | 5.7× cheaper | ## No runtime limits 128 MB is all the memory a Cloudflare Worker gets. OpenOrange runs your Workers and Durable Objects on machines you choose, so the limits are your hardware's. | Limit | Cloudflare Workers Paid | OpenOrange | |---|---|---| | Memory per Worker or Durable Object | 128 MB | Up to your machine's memory. The Node.js heap is up to about 4 GB by default, and configurable. | | CPU time per request | 30 s default, 5 min max | No cap | | Cron, queue and alarm handlers | 15 min wall time | No cap | | Open connections per request | 6 at once | OS limits | | Storage per Durable Object | 10 GB | No cap | | Worker bundle | 64 MiB | No cap | | Node.js | `nodejs_compat` subset | Stock Node.js | ## Architecture

- **Your containers** run your Workers and Durable Objects, in any cloud or on your own servers. - **Rivet** places each Durable Object on a container and routes requests to it. - **S3** stores each object's SQLite data. See [Architecture](https://openorange.dev/docs/architecture/). ## Supported bindings | Cloudflare binding | Status | Runs on | |---|---|---| | [Durable Objects](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/durable-objects/) | Partial | One Rivet Actor for each object, with its own SQLite database | | [KV](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/kv/), [D1](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/d1/), [Rate Limiting](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/rate-limiting/) | Drop-in | Rivet Actors | | [Cache](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/cache/) | Partial | One Rivet Actor for each cache name | | [Queues](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/queues/) | Drop-in | One Rivet Actor for each queue | | [Workflows](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/workflows/) | Partial | Cloudflare's own Workflows engine, with one Rivet Actor for each instance | | [Cron Triggers](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/cron-triggers/) | Drop-in | A Rivet Actor | | [Tail Workers](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/tail-workers/) | Partial | Rivet Durable Streams | | [R2](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/r2/) | Pluggable | A Rivet Actor, or Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, Cloudflare R2 or MinIO | | [Worker Loader](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/worker-loader/) | Partial | A separate process in an agentOS VM | | [Workers AI](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/workers-ai/) | Pluggable | OpenRouter, OpenAI, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint | | [Send Email](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/email/) | Pluggable | Amazon SES, or any SMTP server | | [Browser Rendering](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/browser-rendering/) | Pluggable | Browserbase, or any Chrome DevTools endpoint | | [Hyperdrive](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/hyperdrive/) | Drop-in | Your Postgres or MySQL database, with a direct connection | | [Sandbox](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/sandbox/) | Pluggable | E2B, Daytona, Freestyle, agentOS, or a local directory | | Analytics Engine | Not supported | `writeDataPoint()` drops each data point | | Vectorize, Images, Media, Stream, Pipelines, AI Search, mTLS certificates, VPC, and legacy blobs | Not supported | Calls throw | **Drop-in** runs as on Cloudflare. **Pluggable** runs on a provider you configure. **Partial** runs with known differences, listed on each binding's page. See [binding configuration](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/configuration/) for every Wrangler key and the variables each provider needs, and [Compatibility](https://openorange.dev/docs/compatibility/) for the test results. ## Questions
Wait, wasn't Cloudflare supposed to be cheaper? For small, spiky Workers, it often is: the free tier and per-request pricing are hard to beat. The meters add up once Durable Objects stay busy. The same GB-hours on Graviton EC2 cost about a fifth as much, and writes cost a fraction of that.
Is OpenOrange a fork of Cloudflare? No. OpenOrange implements the Workers API on Node.js and maps each Cloudflare service onto Rivet. It uses Wrangler to read your configuration, and it reuses some MIT-licensed Cloudflare code, such as the Workflows engine. It does not run workerd.
Why not just run workerd directly? workerd is Cloudflare's runtime, not its platform. KV, D1, R2, Queues, Workflows and the Cache API are bindings that call services you have to build, and Durable Objects keep their data on one machine with nothing to place, replicate or scale them. See [OpenOrange vs workerd](https://openorange.dev/vs-workerd/).
Do I need to learn Rivet? No. Rivet is the control plane underneath. You use the `orange` CLI and your Wrangler configuration.
What does it cost? OpenOrange is Apache 2.0 and free. Self-host Rivet and your cloud bill is the only bill. Rivet Cloud and BYOC pricing is at [rivet.dev/pricing](https://rivet.dev/pricing).
What happens to the data already in KV, Durable Objects and R2? `orange migrate` moves Durable Objects while your app serves, with no downtime. D1 databases are interrupted for a few minutes while they copy. R2 is S3-compatible, so `rclone` or `aws s3 sync` moves buckets.
Does it run at the edge? It runs wherever you deploy it, in as many regions as you want. Most backends talk to one database, and running next to it is faster than running at the edge.
Who maintains OpenOrange? [Rivet](https://rivet.dev). OpenOrange is not affiliated with or endorsed by Cloudflare, Inc.
## Compare - [OpenOrange vs Cloudflare Durable Objects](https://openorange.dev/vs-durable-objects/): limits, latency, residency, and moving off. - [OpenOrange vs workerd](https://openorange.dev/vs-workerd/): a runtime for one Worker, versus your whole app in production. - [OpenOrange vs celld](https://openorange.dev/vs-celld/): runtime limits, live migration, integrations, and support. - [OpenOrange vs Rivet](https://openorange.dev/vs-rivet/): when to use Rivet directly, and how to combine them. - [OpenOrange vs Miniflare](https://openorange.dev/vs-miniflare/): a local simulator, versus production. ## Resources - [Deploy guide](https://openorange.dev/docs/deploy/): Rivet Cloud, self-hosting, variables, secrets, and rollback. - [Migration guide](https://openorange.dev/docs/migrate/): how to cut over, how to roll back, and what cannot move. - [Bindings](https://openorange.dev/docs/bindings/): one page for each binding and runtime API, with its known differences. - [Architecture](https://openorange.dev/docs/architecture/): how OpenOrange runs your Worker on Rivet. - [Examples](examples/): Workers that you can copy, with no OpenOrange imports. - [Real projects](packages/cloudflare-conformance/real-projects): open-source Workers run through `orange dev`, with what works and what does not. - [Discord](https://rivet.dev/discord): questions and support. ## License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE)
